blocks.value: The Arrays class (java.util) provides static utility methods for common array tasks — search, compare, fill, and sort. Being static, they're called on the class itself, not on an array object: Arrays.sort(myArray), not myArray.sort().

Method                      Example                      Result
binarySearch(array, key)    Arrays.binarySearch(a, 4)   2 (found at index 2)
binarySearch(array, key)    Arrays.binarySearch(a, 53)  -7 (not found)
equals(array, array)        Arrays.equals(a, b)         false (different contents)
equals(array, array)        Arrays.equals(a, c)         true (same contents)
fill(array, value)          Arrays.fill(a, 8)           every element in a becomes 8
sort(array)                 Arrays.sort(b)              sorts b ascending: {1,2,5,6,7,12}
sort(array, from, to)       Arrays.sort(b, 1, 5)        sorts only indices 1 through 4
Note: binarySearch only gives reliable results on an already-sorted array — sort first if you're not sure the array is in order.
